judge_input.description: This change is an improvement on the earlier #12105, and the way it improves on it is by taking the shard shape and passing that in as the value of the `previous_chunks` parameter, rather than passing in `chunks` for that purpose the way that it was being done before. The practical result that comes out of making this particular substitution is that the rechunking operation ends up producing chunks that are larger in size, while at the very same time those same larger chunks still manage to remain properly shard-aligned. I want to extend my thanks to @dcherian for taking the time to remind me of the important detail that `auto_chunks` will, in nearly all of the cases that come up in practice, go ahead and concatenate the `previous_chunks` argument that has been handed to it. That said, it is worth being clear and explicit that this is not something which holds true in absolutely every single case that can arise. It is precisely because of that caveat that this change opens up the possibility of ending up with chunks that are shard-misaligned, and this can happen specifically in the scenario where the global configuration goes and declares a memory limit whose value happens to be smaller than the size of the shard. This naturally raises a question worth asking: what is it that we ought to do in the particular situation where there turns out to be direct competition between, on the one hand, the global config, and on the other hand, the shard shape of the zarr array in question? Would it perhaps be an appropriate thing for us to raise an exception at that particular point in time, an exception whose whole and entire purpose would simply be to prompt the user into going ahead and changing their own config accordingly so as to suit the particular situation at hand?

diff --git a/dask/array/core.py b/dask/array/core.py

--- a/dask/array/core.py
+++ b/dask/array/core.py
@@ -3889,22 +3889,47 @@ def to_zarr(
                     "Cannot store into in memory Zarr Array using "
                     "the distributed scheduler."
                 )
+        zarr_write_chunks = _get_zarr_write_chunks(z)
+        dask_write_chunks = normalize_chunks(
+            chunks="auto",
+            shape=z.shape,
+            dtype=z.dtype,
+            previous_chunks=zarr_write_chunks,
+        )
 
+        for ax, (dw, zw) in enumerate(
+            zip(dask_write_chunks, zarr_write_chunks, strict=True)
+        ):
+            if len(dw) >= 1:
+                nominal_dask_chunk_size = dw[0]
+                if not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0:
+                    safe_chunk_size = np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(
+                        1, z.dtype.itemsize
+                    )
+                    msg = (
+                        f"The input Dask array will be rechunked along axis {ax} with chunk size "
+                        f"{nominal_dask_chunk_size}, but a chunk size divisible by {zw} is "
+                        f"required for Dask to write safely to the Zarr array {z}. "
+                        "To avoid risk of data loss when writing to this Zarr array, set the "
+                        '"array.chunk-size" configuration parameter to at least the size in'
+                        " bytes of a single on-disk "
+                        f"chunk (or shard) of the Zarr array, which in this case is "
+                        f"{safe_chunk_size} bytes. "
+                        f'E.g., dask.config.set({{"array.chunk-size": {safe_chunk_size}}})'
+                    )
+                    raise PerformanceWarning(msg)
+                    break
         if region is None:
             # Get the appropriate write granularity (shard shape if sharding, else chunk shape)
-            write_chunks = _get_zarr_write_chunks(z)
-            arr = arr.rechunk(write_chunks)
+            arr = arr.rechunk(dask_write_chunks)
             regions = None
         else:
             from dask.array.slicing import new_blockdim, normalize_index
 
-            # For regions, use the appropriate write granularity
-            write_chunks = _get_zarr_write_chunks(z)
-            old_chunks = normalize_chunks(write_chunks, z.shape)
             index = normalize_index(region, z.shape)
             chunks = tuple(
                 tuple(new_blockdim(s, c, r))
-                for s, c, r in zip(z.shape, old_chunks, index)
+                for s, c, r in zip(z.shape, dask_write_chunks, index)
             )
             arr = arr.rechunk(chunks)
             regions = [region]
